quote: The present report is submitted pursuant to General Assembly resolution 78/311
summary: The supplied draft describes its reporting mandate as resolution 78/311's request for a Secretary-General report at the eightieth session on developing-country AI capacity challenges and recommendations.
document_status: Draft Secretary-General report; not an adopted decision or final report.

quote: This includes gaps in foundational AI capacity such as in compute, associated energy and connectivity needs, high-quality data, in digital public infrastructure, model use case repositories, and in skills for AI development and deployment.
summary: The draft distinguishes foundational AI inputs from enabling capacity in regulation, public-sector procurement and governance, accountability, and international participation.
document_status: Draft analysis of developing-country capacity needs.

quote: initial funding commitments in the range of $3 billion over four years
summary: The draft proposes a needs-based global AI capacity fund at this initial financing scale, complementing existing mechanisms and supporting nationally owned development priorities. It does not establish or demonstrate funding of such a fund.
document_status: Draft funding proposal; not an established or funded mechanism.

quote: There was a strong focus among G77 nations on the need to harness existing and frontier technologies to advance development alongside an emphasis from many developed countries on the need for risk mitigation and effective governance of digital and tech.
summary: The September 2024 SPMU summary offers historical framing of development-oriented technology priorities alongside risk mitigation and governance priorities; this is not evidence of current-session positions.
document_status: Historical UNGA 79 SPMU background summary, September 2024.

quote: Scraping speech summaries from the gadebate.un.org website
summary: The historical SPMU account used scraped speech summaries, then text analysis, human interpretation, SPMU classification and comparison with dig.watch. Its methodology should be distinguished from full-text review of the current corpus.
document_status: Historical methodology description in the September 2024 SPMU summary.

quote:
operating under a strictly scientific, non-political mandate to document international 
scientific consensus and disagreements while remaining policy-relevant but not 
policy-prescriptive.
summary: The July 2026 preliminary report describes the Panel as established by General Assembly resolution 79/325 in 2025 and serving a scientific, non-political mandate. Members serve personally; the preliminary assessment is intended for progressive revision and does not represent official UN or government views.
document_status: Preliminary independent scientific report, July 2026; not a policy prescription or official government position.

quote:
the only standing 
United Nations mechanism with a mandate for 
regular scientific assessment of the state, risks and 
capabilities of AI
summary: The preliminary report describes the Panel as a standing UN scientific assessment mechanism designed for sustained, iterative work. Its role is to document evidence, consensus, disagreements and gaps while remaining policy-relevant but not policy-prescriptive.
document_status: Preliminary scientific report, July 2026; institutional self-description at publication.

quote:
Most countries, including 
many advanced economies, lack the technical expertise to assess the most capable
summary: The report identifies uneven national capacity to assess frontier models and participate in their governance, with evaluation expertise, compute and language data concentrated where AI is developed.
document_status: Preliminary scientific assessment, July 2026; capacity finding.

quote: Access to AI tools alone does not produce equal benefit
summary: Effective and safe AI deployment also depends on complementary investment in data, skills, workflows and institutions; the Panel presents its preliminary evidence base as one contribution to building Member State capacity.
document_status: Preliminary scientific assessment, July 2026; not a funding commitment.

quote:
these thresholds remain defined by the developers, 
without standardized evaluation or external 
verification
summary: The report cites developer-defined risk thresholds and fragmented regional governance as reasons for independent scientific assessment and shared evidence standards.
document_status: Preliminary scientific assessment, July 2026; diagnosis rather than an adopted governance rule.

quote: Foundation models and task-specific AI.
summary: The report primarily addresses broadly capable foundation and general-purpose models deployed at scale, while distinguishing narrower systems whose usefulness depends on defined tasks, available data and institutional deployment capacity.
document_status: Preliminary scientific report, July 2026; stated analytical scope.

quote:
government experts primarily receive the testing 
data that developers choose to share.
summary: The preliminary assessment identifies an information imbalance in AI safety validation: developers largely design their own evaluations, making standardized independent assessment and better-resourced measurement important capacity needs.
document_status: Preliminary scientific assessment, July 2026.

quote:
many 
decisions about training data, safeguards, 
deployment thresholds, model access and 
capability release sit inside private firms.
summary: The report links concentrated AI inputs and business-led frontier development to private control over important governance choices. Its numerical development and compute comparisons are explicitly dated to 2025.
document_status: Preliminary scientific assessment using dated 2025 evidence; not current speech counts.

quote:
Inclusion requires targeted 
investment, public data sets and benchmark 
initiatives for underrepresented linguistic and 
cultural contexts
summary: The report identifies linguistic inclusion and more geographically representative evaluation as capacity needs, observing that evidence is concentrated in high-income English-language settings.
document_status: Preliminary scientific assessment, July 2026.

quote:
Multi-
stakeholder financing, including the Global Fund on AI 
proposed by the UN Secretary-General, may help.
summary: The report presents pooled data, capital, compute, energy and talent as possible responses to dependence on foreign AI infrastructure, and refers to the Global Fund as a proposal rather than an established funding mechanism.
document_status: Preliminary scientific report describing a financing proposal.

quote:
Building national and regional AI 
safety institutes and technical secondments 
for regulators may help to build capacity.
summary: National and regional safety institutes, regulator secondments and evaluation adapted to low-resource languages are presented as possible ways to strengthen governance capacity.
document_status: Preliminary scientific assessment of possible capacity measures; not an adopted mandate.

quote:
Governments have 
committed to promoting AI literacy in the Global 
Digital Compact
summary: The report places AI literacy alongside institutional capacity, data, training, regulation and workflow redesign as necessary complements to access, and cites a literacy commitment in the Global Digital Compact.
document_status: Preliminary scientific report referring to the Global Digital Compact commitment.

quote:
AI literacy should be understood as a complement to, 
not a substitute for, developer responsibility, institutional safeguards and regulatory accountability.
summary: The preliminary report identifies gaps in AI literacy frameworks, independent evaluation and adoption across schools and professional training. It treats literacy as institutional capacity building alongside developer and regulatory responsibility.
document_status: Preliminary scientific assessment, July 2026; not an adopted education programme.

quote:
Oversight 
is not yet operationalized as a measurable 
requirement with concrete expectations for 
intervention, reversibility and accountability
summary: The report identifies a governance capacity gap for autonomous agents and calls for measurable human oversight, evaluation and interoperability standards, critical-infrastructure collaboration, and clearer attribution in liability and incident reporting.
document_status: Preliminary scientific assessment of institutional preparedness needs.

quote:
National strategies to address disinformation 
and persuasion are an exception.
summary: The report identifies limited national preparedness for AI-enabled persuasion and disinformation, arguing that governance must address the incentives and infrastructure that make manipulation profitable as well as content moderation.
document_status: Preliminary scientific assessment, July 2026; not evidence of a new adopted national strategy.

quote:
Human rights due diligence, impact 
assessments and rights-by-design approaches 
provide established tools
summary: The report frames human-rights and child-rights impact assessment as existing instruments that can be applied across the AI lifecycle, while identifying transparency and explainability gaps that impede accountability and remedies.
document_status: Preliminary scientific assessment of available governance tools.

quote:
there is a critical need 
for rigorous auditability and transparent data 
lineage that connects every generated claim 
back to reliable evidence.
summary: The preliminary report identifies auditable human-AI workflows and explicit criteria for escalation to human oversight as governance requirements. Its short-, medium- and long-term trajectories are possible futures rather than completed developments.
document_status: Preliminary scientific assessment containing prospective scenarios, July 2026.

quote:
These gains are real but 
conditional: they depend on local contextualization, 
adequate infrastructure, and human preparation.
summary: The preliminary report links benefits in science, health, education and agriculture to local context, infrastructure and human preparation, identifying teacher readiness and digital capacity gaps as barriers to equitable deployment.
document_status: Preliminary scientific assessment of sectoral capacity needs.

quote:
Agricultural AI systems are most sustainable 
when treated as shared public infrastructure 
with clear governance
summary: The report frames agricultural AI as shared public infrastructure and states that sustained anticipatory food-security impact depends on embedding solutions in national institutions and accounting for smallholder conditions.
document_status: Preliminary scientific assessment of institutional conditions for agricultural AI.

quote:
The evidence base is biased toward advanced 
economies, large firms and formal work.
summary: The report cautions that economic findings concentrated in advanced economies and formal digital work may not generalize to developing economies. Productivity gains require complementary investments in data, skills and organizational change.
document_status: Preliminary scientific assessment; evidence limitation rather than a universal economic forecast.

quote:
unless national 
statistical systems are updated and are 
given additional access for measurement by 
AI developers.
summary: The report identifies updated statistical systems and additional developer access as prerequisites for measuring AI's effects on jobs, wages, productivity, trade and distribution, with privacy-preserving and cost-conscious methods.
document_status: Preliminary scientific assessment of measurement capacity needs.

quote:
The Global South is disproportionately exposed 
due to structural vulnerabilities.
summary: The preliminary report identifies reliance on foreign software, limited resilience and mitigation capacity, and local data gaps as structural sources of unequal exposure; it also notes disproportionate environmental and socioeconomic impacts in the global South.
document_status: Preliminary scientific assessment, July 2026.

quote:
questions surrounding model access controls, vulnerability disclosure norms, and the 
equitable deployment of AI tools, particularly in developing economies, are increasingly becoming matters 
of international policy
summary: The report frames access to defensive AI capabilities and vulnerability disclosure as international governance and equity issues, noting that developers' restricted releases concentrate safety and access decisions within a select coalition.
document_status: Preliminary scientific assessment of reported capability restrictions; not an adopted international access regime.

quote:
Transparency and accountability are key 
pillars for meaningful access to justice.
summary: The report identifies insufficient system transparency and explainability as barriers to developer and deployer accountability, the rule of law and remedies for human-rights violations.
document_status: Preliminary scientific assessment of institutional accountability needs.

quote: The determination remains the subject of ongoing legal dispute
summary: The report explicitly treats the election-annulment example and the role of platform amplification as contested. Its 2023-2024 election examples provide dated background on governance risks, not proof of later events or definitive causal attribution to AI.
document_status: Preliminary scientific report describing dated, partly contested electoral cases.

quote:
It also requires investments in AI 
capacity, infrastructure, and skills across 
countries and regions, as well as more 
representative data and benchmarks.
summary: The report frames inclusive AI as requiring both representative local data and capacity investment, alongside changes in who develops, defines, owns and governs AI systems.
document_status: Preliminary scientific assessment of inclusion and capacity needs.

quote:
Evaluation and measurement are key capacities 
for effective AI governance but are critically 
underdeveloped
summary: The preliminary scientific report identifies evaluation and measurement as underdeveloped governance capacities, requiring context-sensitive assessment of deployed systems, not models alone.
document_status: Preliminary scientific report; assessment, not an adopted governance instrument

quote:
A United Nations-based platform is also 
one promising option to host this dialogue 
on a continuous, universally inclusive basis, 
complementary to the venues above.
summary: The Panel discusses a continuous, inclusive UN platform for developer-state-scientist dialogue as complementary to other venues; this passage proposes a function rather than granting enforcement powers.
document_status: Preliminary scientific report; governance assessment and proposal

quote:
Significant global capacity-building is required to ensure local communities can safely adapt and 
assess AI systems.
summary: Open models offer adaptation and innovation opportunities but require local assessment capacity and safeguards against irreversible release and misuse.
document_status: Preliminary scientific report; scientific assessment

quote:
activities of the Panel and the 
Dialogue are limited to the non-military domain and do 
not refer to artificial intelligence for military purposes
summary: The report explicitly identifies the Panel and Dialogue mandate under resolution79/325 as non-military; military AI and lethal autonomous weapons fall outside its present scope.
document_status: Preliminary report citing an adopted General Assembly resolution

quote:
General Assembly resolution 
79/325 explicitly provides for the issuance of 
thematic briefs in addition to the annual report.
summary: The report describes thematic briefs as part of the mandate and planned follow-up work; intended briefs are not evidence of later publication.
document_status: Preliminary report; mandate description and planned next steps

quote:
The Independent International Scientific Panel on Artificial Intelligence was established within the United Nations 
through General Assembly resolution 79/325, as committed to through the Global Digital Compact and the Pact for the 
Future.
summary: The supplied report states that General Assembly resolution 79/325 established the Panel within the UN, following commitments in the Global Digital Compact and Pact for the Future.
document_status: Preliminary scientific report; institutional description, not an adopted intergovernmental decision

quote: Composed of 40 independent experts appointed by the General Assembly for a term of three years
summary: The report describes a Panel of 40 independent experts appointed by the General Assembly for three-year terms; it also states that membership is gender balanced and drawn from all five regional groups and multiple disciplines.
document_status: Preliminary scientific report; institutional description, not an adopted intergovernmental decision

quote:
The Panel is mandated to issue evidence-based scientific assessments synthesizing and analysing existing 
research related to the opportunities, risks and impacts of AI through an annual policy-relevant but non-prescriptive 
summary report including thematic briefs as it deems necessary.
summary: The Panel's described mandate is to synthesize existing research on AI opportunities, risks and impacts in an annual policy-relevant, non-prescriptive report, with thematic briefs as needed.
document_status: Preliminary scientific report; institutional description, not an adopted intergovernmental decision

quote:
The Panel is also mandated to present its annual summary report at the United Nations Global Dialogue on Artificial 
Intelligence Governance.
summary: The described mandate requires presentation of the annual summary report at the UN Global Dialogue on AI Governance; this mandate alone does not establish that any later presentation occurred.
document_status: Preliminary scientific report; institutional description, not an adopted intergovernmental decision

quote:
In the three months since the Panel’s first meeting in March 2026, following their appointment in February 2026, the 
Panel worked intensively to deliver the present report.
summary: The report dates the experts' appointment to February 2026 and their first meeting to March 2026, describing three months of preparation. It characterizes the present document as a preliminary baseline for wider consultation and subsequent thematic briefs and annual reports.
document_status: Preliminary scientific report describing its own preparation chronology and prospective follow-up

quote: Panel members serve in their personal capacity as scientifically independent experts.
summary: Members serve personally as independent scientific experts. The supplied text further states that, as UN experts on mission, they pledged not to seek or accept government or other outside instructions in performing their duties.
document_status: Preliminary scientific report; institutional description, not an adopted intergovernmental decision

quote:
The Panel Secretariat gratefully acknowledges the financial and in-kind contributions of the following governments 
and partners
summary: The supplied Panel report acknowledges Germany, Japan, Spain and Omidyar Network Fund as contributors. These are background acknowledgements, not General Debate pledge counts.
document_status: Supplied preliminary report; donor acknowledgements

quote: The first session of the Global Dialogue on AI Governance was held on 6 and 7 July 2026 in Geneva.
summary: The official Dialogue website reports that the first session took place in Geneva on6?7July2026. This indexed excerpt provides a dated event confirmation, not evidence of every proposed outcome.
document_status: Official website content accessed through search index on29September2026; direct fetch403

quote: the General Assembly endorse the need for, and take steps to advance, the establishment of a Global Fund for AI Capacity-Building
summary: The official ODET announcement recommends advancing establishment of a Global Fund for AI Capacity-Building; it does not establish that a fund has been created or financed.
document_status: Official website recommendation accessed through search index on29September2026; direct fetch403

quote: NEW YORK, 1 July 2026 - The UN Independent International Scientific Panel on Artificial Intelligence today officially released its Preliminary Report
summary: The official UN notice dates release of the preliminary Panel report to1July2026. Its scientific assessment should not be described as binding rules.
